Summarize and Visualize C-index Results from Survival Model Cross-Validation

Source: R/machine_learning.R
compute_cv_CINDEX.Rd

This function summarizes and visualizes the C-index (concordance index) results obtained from survival model cross-validation, typically produced by cross_validation_custom(). It computes median C-index and MAD (median absolute deviation) per model, ranks models by performance, and generates a bar plot showing median C-index ± MAD for easy comparison.

Usage

compute_cv_CINDEX(surv_results, file_name = NULL, return = TRUE)

Arguments

surv_results

A data frame or tibble containing the summarized cross-validation performance results for each survival model. It must include the following columns:

model

Model name or identifier (character).

median

Median C-index across folds (numeric).

mad

Median absolute deviation of C-index (numeric).

file_name

Optional character string used to name the output PDF file saved under "Results/CINDEX_CV_methods_<file_name>.pdf". If NULL, the file name is omitted or handled by default behavior.

return

Logical; if TRUE (default), the plot is generated and saved as a PDF in the "Results/" directory.

Value

A list containing two elements:

CINDEX_summary

A tibble summarizing model performance (median and MAD).

Top_model

Character string indicating the model with the highest median C-index.

Details

The plot displays:

  • Bars = Median C-index per model.

  • Error bars = ± MAD (robust variability).

The output allows easy visual comparison of survival models based on their discriminative performance.

See also

cross_validation_custom()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
results <- tibble::tibble(
  model = c("cox_ph_survival", "rand_forest_aorsf"),
  median = c(0.78, 0.82),
  mad = c(0.03, 0.02)
)
compute_cv_CINDEX(results, file_name = "example")
} # }
